title: Right-click menu reads 'Move to folderâ€¦' - a double-encoded ellipsis
body:
## Summary
The shelf's context menu labels its first (default-focused) item with mojibake: the UTF-8 bytes of '…' were decoded as cp1252 and re-encoded, so the menu renders 'Move to folderâ€¦' and 'Move 3 to folderâ€¦'.

## Description
app/library/assets/ShelfDialogs.tsx:93-94 hold the bytes c3 a2 e2 82 ac c2 a6 (od -c) where every sibling label uses U+2026 ('Add reference…' ShelfGallery.tsx:110, 'Move to folder…' ShelfGallery.tsx:146). Introduced in e1dd749 (2026-09-09). A whole-tree scan of tracked app/components/lib sources for the double-encoding signature finds exactly these two lines and nothing else, so a ratchet costs nothing to hold at zero. ContextMenu focuses its FIRST item on open (ContextMenu.tsx:62-67), so this is the label a screen reader announces first and a sighted user reads first.

## Flow
- Right-click any tile on Library > Assets
- Menu opens with focus on item 1: 'Move to folderâ€¦'
- Select several tiles, right-click inside the selection: 'Move 3 to folderâ€¦'

## Expected impact
Every refile via the context menu shows a broken string in the default item; the bulk move and the keyboard path announce it. One-line fix plus a tree-wide guard so an editor round-trip cannot reintroduce it.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - the context-menu move item reads as a broken string, and it is the first thing announced when the menu opens
Before: 2 mojibake sites in tracked sources (ShelfDialogs.tsx:93, :94); 0 probes guard source encoding
After: 0 sites; a probe fails on any new double-encoded sequence
Method: probe - python scan of `git ls-files app components lib` (.ts/.tsx/.css/.mjs) for /\u00e2\u20ac|\u00c3[\u0080-\u00bf]/ returned exactly ShelfDialogs.tsx:93 and :94; bytes confirmed with od -c
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence: app/library/assets/ShelfDialogs.tsx:93 `Move ${chosen.length} to folderâ€¦`; :94 "Move to folderâ€¦"; od -c shows 303 242 342 202 254 302 246; tree scan hits = 2 (both here); sibling ShelfGallery.tsx:146 'Move to folder…' is correct; last touched e1dd749
verify: Write tests/golden-path/source-encoding.probe.spec.ts first: walk app/, components/, lib/ (readdirSync recursion as object-url-ownership.probe.spec.ts does) for .ts/.tsx/.css/.mjs, read utf-8, assert no match of /\u00e2\u20ac|\u00c3[\u0080-\u00bf]/ and report file:line - RED on HEAD listing ShelfDialogs.tsx:93,94. Replace both with U+2026; probe GREEN; npm run typecheck.

title: A shelf that failed to load says 'The shelf is empty' and the Assets tab reads 0
body:
## Summary
When the shelf cannot be read, the gallery renders the read error AND the zero-rows empty state beneath it ('The shelf is empty', an empty-tile Ghost, an 'open Styles' call to action), and the Library tab rail's Assets tally drops to 0.

## Description
lib/useAssets.ts:214-216 sets `assets = []` alongside `error` on a failed read. useShelf.ts:99 guards the count with the comment 'still reading - an unknown count is not 0', but only for `null`; after a failure `rows.length` is 0 and onCount(0) fires (useShelf.ts:100), so LibraryView.tsx:103 draws a 0 tally (it omits the tally only for undefined). ShelfGallery.tsx:61-76 draws the alert + retry, then :166-167 renders <EmptyShelf hasAny={false}> on `shown.length === 0` with no error term, which asserts 'The shelf is empty' (EmptyShelf.tsx:29) and offers to go fill it (EmptyShelf.tsx:37-41). FAILURE and ZERO ROWS therefore render the same body; only the alert differs, and the body below it contradicts the alert. The comment at useShelf.ts:99 is the spec; the failure path breaks it.

## Flow
- IndexedDB read throws (quota, private window, blocked storage)
- Alert: '<message>' + retry
- Directly below: 'The shelf is empty' + Ghost + 'open Styles'
- Tab rail: Assets 0

## Expected impact
A user whose plates exist but could not be read is told they have none and invited to recreate them. The fix makes failure render as failure: alert + retry only, and no tally.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - a failed read is shown as an empty shelf with a call to refill it, and the tab count claims 0
Before: read failure renders 3 empty-state assertions (heading, Ghost label, CTA) plus tally 0; failure and empty share 1 body branch
After: read failure renders the alert + retry only; tally omitted (undefined); 2 distinct branches
Method: probe - code read of the render branch: useAssets.ts:215 -> rows [] -> ShelfGallery.tsx:166 ternary has no error term; useShelf.ts:99-100 guards only null
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence: lib/useAssets.ts:214-216 (catch: setAssets([]); setError(...)); app/library/assets/useShelf.ts:99 comment 'an unknown count is not 0', :100 onCount(rows.length); app/library/assets/ShelfGallery.tsx:61-76 alert, :166-167 `shown.length === 0 ? <EmptyShelf hasAny={rows.length > 0} .../>`; app/library/assets/EmptyShelf.tsx:29, :37-41; app/library/LibraryView.tsx:103 tally only when counts.assets !== undefined
verify: Add to app/library/assets/shelf.ts (no React) `export function galleryState(a: {error: string | null; total: number; shown: number}): 'failed' | 'empty' | 'grid'` ('failed' when error && total === 0) and `export function shelfCount(a: {loaded: boolean; error: string | null; total: number}): number | undefined` (undefined when !loaded, or error && total === 0). Probe imports both from '@/app/library/assets/shelf' and asserts galleryState({error:'x',total:0,shown:0}) === 'failed', ({error:null,total:0,shown:0}) === 'empty', ({error:'x',total:5,shown:5}) === 'grid', shelfCount({loaded:true,error:'x',total:0}) === undefined - RED on HEAD (no export). Then ShelfGallery.tsx renders EmptyShelf only for 'empty' (nothing extra for 'failed'; the alert already renders), and useShelf.ts's onCount effect calls onCount only when shelfCount(...) !== undefined. The same probe source-ratchets (stripComments) that ShelfGallery.tsx contains `galleryState(` and useShelf.ts contains `shelfCount(`. npm run typecheck; npm test.

title: Audio workbench sets 26 text colours in --al-ash; an unscored cell is 1.9:1
body:
## Summary
tokens.ts states that `--al-ash` is not a text colour; the kit's own CSS obeys that (0 text uses) while its port, audio-workbench.css, uses ash for text 26 times - and the rubric's unscored marker multiplies it by opacity .5 down to about 1.9:1 on ink.

## Description
components/ui/tokens.ts:229-231: 'TEXT HAS TWO LEVELS, `white` and `vellum`, and nothing else ... `ash` is NOT a text colour ... it draws rings, rules and the rejected disc.' Under the Obsidian kit world the workbench mounts (AudioWorkbench.tsx:553 world='obsidian'), tokens.ts:290 resolves ash to ink-bright #f3f6fb at 45% over ink #080a10 = rgb(114,116,122) -> 4.24:1, under WCAG AA 4.5:1 for the 1rem text it colours (column heads :148/:151, tally units :61, caps labels :107, tab labels :231, facts dt :255, rubric labels :243, rubric digits :246, the unjudged verdict pill :189, the take id :239). `.ab .sc.na { color: var(--al-ash); opacity: 0.5 }` (:194) composites to rgb(61,63,69) -> 1.88:1: that is the middle dot Ledger.tsx:186 draws for every rubric score not yet given and the 'n/a' at :185 - the marker of the work still to do on a scoring surface, drawn near the invisible-Ghost threshold this repo already shipped once. PAIR: components/kit/*.css colours no text with ash (0 uses; the kit draws ash only as hairlines/strokes). Vellum in the same world = ink-bright 72% -> about 9:1.

## Flow
- Library > Audio, any width
- Ledger: MEL/CHO/QUA cells with no score show a middle dot at ~1.9:1
- Column heads, tally units, facts labels, the unjudged pill: ~4.2:1

## Expected impact
The unscored state becomes legible and every label clears AA; the port is brought onto the token contract its own header claims ('COLOUR IS TOKENS ONLY').

## Evaluation
Claim: user - unscored rubric cells and most labels in the audio ledger are below AA contrast on the ink ground
Before: 26 `color: var(--al-ash)` text declarations in audio-workbench.css, 0 in components/kit/*.css; ash text 4.24:1; .sc.na 1.88:1 (sRGB composite over #080a10, WCAG relative luminance)
After: 0 ash text declarations (vellum ~9:1 for secondary text, white for primary); .sc.na has no opacity and reads >= 4.5:1
Method: probe - grep count over the CSS, and contrast computed from tokens.ts INK #080a10 / INK_BRIGHT #f3f6fb with WORLD_OBSIDIAN_KIT --al-ash 45% / --al-vellum 72%
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence: components/ui/tokens.ts:229-231 (ash is NOT a text colour), :290 --al-ash = color-mix(ink-bright 45%, transparent), :289 vellum 72%, :105 INK #080a10, :111 INK_BRIGHT #f3f6fb; app/library/audio/audio-workbench.css lines 52,61,107,113,120,132,148,151,170,189,194,206,227,231,239,243,246,255,267,279,294,296,319,321,324,330 match /[^-]color: var\(--al-ash\)/ (26); :194 `.sc.na { color: var(--al-ash); opacity: 0.5 }`; app/library/audio/Ledger.tsx:185-186 'n/a' and the middle dot render with class `sc na`; components/kit/*.css text-colour ash uses = 0
verify: Probe first: read app/library/audio/audio-workbench.css, strip /* */ comments, count /(^|[;{\s])color:\s*var\(--al-ash\)/g (does not match border-color) and expect 0 - RED on HEAD at 26; also assert the `.ab .sc.na` rule body contains no `opacity`. Then replace each text `color: var(--al-ash)` with `color: var(--al-vellum)` (hierarchy rides on white vs vellum, per tokens.ts:229) and drop `opacity: 0.5` from .sc.na; keep `.path li.ghost::after { border-color: var(--al-ash) }` (a rule, allowed). GREEN. Then photograph per CLAUDE.md with pipeline/cx-capture.mjs (the library audio screen id from its list) at 1920 and confirm the dot cells read and column heads still sit below titles in weight.

title: Closed Inspector/Terms drawers stay in the Tab order on narrow screens
body:
## Summary
Under 1000px the Inspector column, and under 720px the Terms column, become off-canvas drawers by CSS transform only. Closed, they remain focusable: Tab walks a keyboard user through dozens of controls that sit 105% off-screen, with the focus ring invisible.

## Description
audio-workbench.css:343 `.ab-col--right { position: fixed; ... transform: translateX(105%) }` (opened by .drawer-open, :344) and :349 `.ab-col--left { ... transform: translateX(-105%) }` (opened by .terms-open, :350). Nothing removes the closed column from the focus order: AudioWorkbench.tsx:709 and :812 render both <aside>s with no `inert`, `hidden` or tabIndex handling, and no component in app/ or components/ uses an `inert` attribute (grep). The right column holds the Take/Compose tabs, the close button, 30 rubric radio buttons (Inspector.tsx:159-173), Keep/Reject/Clear/Seed, the composer's term inputs, tempo/key, the target toggle, Copy, and a Dropzone per draft - 40+ stops, all invisible when closed. Escape closes the drawer (AudioWorkbench.tsx:382-384) but nothing returns focus to the 'Inspector'/'Terms' toggle that opened it. The surface plainly targets narrow use: it ships the drawers, a scrim and `only-narrow` toggles (audio-workbench.css:98, :342).

## Flow
- Viewport 900px, Library > Audio
- Tab past the ledger
- Focus enters the off-screen Inspector: ~40 Tab presses with no visible focus before the page continues
- Press O (opens the drawer), then Esc: focus stays where it was, possibly inside the now-hidden column

## Expected impact
Keyboard users on laptops/tablets under 1000px stop losing focus into invisible UI; the drawer behaves like the overlay it visually is.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - on a narrow screen, Tab disappears into a closed drawer for dozens of presses
Before: 0 of 2 off-canvas columns removed from the focus order when closed; >= 40 hidden tab stops in the closed Inspector
After: closed drawers carry `inert` at their breakpoints (0 hidden stops); Esc/scrim/close return focus to the toggle
Method: probe - code read: transform-only hiding at audio-workbench.css:343,349; asides at AudioWorkbench.tsx:709,812 carry no inert/hidden; grep for an inert attribute in app/components .tsx = 0
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence: app/library/audio/audio-workbench.css:340-351 (transform-only drawers at max-width 999px / 720px); app/library/audio/AudioWorkbench.tsx:709 <aside className="ab-col ab-col--left">, :812 <aside ref={rightRef} className="ab-col ab-col--right">, :382-384 Esc closes without focus return, :601-608 and :697-704 toggles; app/library/audio/Inspector.tsx:159-173 (30 radio buttons); grep -rn inert app components --include=*.tsx -> no attribute use
verify: Probe first (source ratchet, stripComments): AudioWorkbench.tsx must contain the media strings '(max-width: 999px)' and '(max-width: 720px)' (the probe also reads audio-workbench.css and asserts it still uses those two breakpoints, so the pair cannot drift), and both the ab-col--left and ab-col--right <aside> elements must carry an `inert={` prop whose expression mentions `drawer` - RED on HEAD. Implement: two matchMedia-backed booleans (subscribe to change), `inert={narrowLeft && drawer !== "terms"}` on the left aside and `inert={narrowRight && drawer !== "inspector"}` on the right (React 19.2 accepts boolean inert); remember the toggle that opened a drawer and focus it on close (Esc, scrim, close button). GREEN; npm run typecheck.

title: A later save erases the notice that an earlier audio judgment was not saved
body:
## Summary
useAudioShelf keeps ONE error string for the whole shelf, and every successful write clears it. A failed verdict save on take A is wiped by the next successful save on take B: the alert disappears while take A still shows its verdict locally, and loses it on reload.

## Description
useAudioShelf.ts:112 applies the patch to the local row first; on failure :115 sets 'The last judgment was not saved: ... A reload would lose it.' - a real error that correctly states its consequence. But :128 `setError(null)` runs on ANY later patch success, for any take; :156 (a filed return) and :172 (clearing examples) do the same. The same single slot also holds the read failure (:75) and the migration report (:82-88, 'N of this browser's takes did not move to the studio shelf'), so one successful keypress also erases a migration failure. AudioWorkbench.tsx:541 and :692-696 render whatever is in the slot as role=alert. Judging runs at keyboard speed (Enter/X advance to the next take, AudioWorkbench.tsx:279-294), so the next save follows within a second: the failure notice is effectively never readable, and nothing marks WHICH take is unsaved.

## Flow
- Patch for take A fails (network, 5xx)
- Alert: 'The last judgment was not saved ... A reload would lose it.'
- User presses Enter on take B a second later; B saves
- Alert cleared; A still reads 'kept' in the ledger; reload -> A is unjudged again

## Expected impact
Lost human judgments become visible and attributable; the read and migration reports survive unrelated writes.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - a verdict that failed to save is silently forgotten as soon as the next one succeeds
Before: 1 failed + 1 later successful patch -> 0 notices on screen, 1 verdict lost on reload, no take marked
After: the notice persists (keyed to take A) until A's own patch succeeds; read/migration notices are not cleared by writes
Method: simulation - walked the state transitions in useAudioShelf.ts:105-131; not driven (the hook needs a React harness and a failing patchTake)
Result: unmeasurable
Gate: none
evidence: app/library/audio/useAudioShelf.ts:58 single `error` state; :75 read failure; :82-88 migration report; :115 'The last judgment was not saved'; :128 setError(null) on any patch success; :151/:156 upload; :168/:172 clear; app/library/audio/AudioWorkbench.tsx:541 storageError = shelf.error ?? bookError, :692-696 role=alert, :279-294 verdictThen advances immediately
verify: Extract the error bookkeeping into a pure reducer (in useAudioShelf.ts or a sibling .ts): errors keyed by source ('read' | 'migrate' | `patch:${id}` | 'upload' | 'clear'); a patch success clears only its own `patch:${id}` key. Probe drives the reducer: fail patch A then succeed patch B -> A's notice still present (RED against the single-slot model); succeed A -> cleared; succeed B -> 'migrate' untouched. Lane B because useAudioShelf.ts is outside this context's mapped file_paths.

lens_checked.visual-craft: Read in full: AssetsBrowser.tsx, AssetLightbox.tsx, ContextMenu.tsx, FolderTree.tsx, MoveDialog.tsx, assets/{EmptyShelf,ShelfDialogs,ShelfGallery,Tile}.tsx, assets/useShelf.ts, audio/{AudioWorkbench,Inspector,Ledger,Terms,References,RejectBox,PlayButton}.tsx, audio/audio-workbench.css, audio/useAudioShelf.ts; components/ui/signal README + tokens.ts WORLD_OBSIDIAN_KIT (contrast computed for --al-ash/--al-vellum); kit CSS grep for ash-as-text (0). Tile TEXT badge (Tile.tsx:114) and AssetLightbox TEXT badge (:194) share one spelling.
lens_checked.ux-reviewer: Shelf removal paths (Tile Delete, context menu, viewer, bulk) all move focus and announce (useShelf.ts:205-275); upload refusals are named (useShelf.ts:351). Audio keyboard loop (AudioWorkbench.tsx:379-445), drafts/attach, clipboard-blocked toast (:328-334). Noted, not emitted: bulk 'Remove' (ShelfGallery.tsx:148-154) deletes N plates with no confirm or undo although removal is permanent (Tile.tsx:63-68) - a product call between confirm and undo.
lens_checked.state-coverage: useAssets read/remove/move errors vs ShelfGallery branches (finding 2); useAudioShelf read/patch/upload/clear vs AudioWorkbench/Ledger (finding 5). Noted, not emitted: Ledger `0 / {corpus}` (Ledger.tsx:409) is one rendering for an empty shelf, a failed read and a filter excluding everything; audio onCount(0) after a failed read (AudioWorkbench.tsx:167) is the twin of finding 2 but needs useAudioShelf (unmapped) to tell read failure from a save failure.
lens_checked.copy-auditor: Whole-tree mojibake scan (2 hits, finding 1); shelf vs audio vocabulary (plate/reference/take) consistent within each surface; MoveDialog 'letters or numbers, please' is a rule, kept; Inspector 'one axis each' (Inspector.tsx:417) is a 3-word caption about the panel, borderline narration, not emitted.
lens_checked.accessibility-checker: Noted, not emitted (budget): Tile role=button aria-label (Tile.tsx:43) overrides its children, so the TEXT leakage flag (:113-117) is never announced; FolderTree's selected folder is colour-only (FolderTree.tsx:232-238, no aria-current/aria-pressed on the row button :261) while MoveDialog's twin list uses aria-pressed (:134); the Inspector tablist is hand-rolled (AudioWorkbench.tsx:814-821, role=tab without aria-controls/tabpanel/arrow keys) although <TabRail> exists; Ledger <tr aria-selected> sits in a plain table (Ledger.tsx:552); the rubric radiogroup is 30 tab stops with no roving (Inspector.tsx:159-173).

lens_no_surface.mobile-specialist: The shelf grid is responsive by Tailwind breakpoints and the audio workbench ships explicit drawers; the one narrow defect found is filed under accessibility (finding 4).

map_drift: context-map.json lists app/library/audio/TakeExpansion.tsx and VocabSpine.tsx, which do not exist (stale); Terms.tsx, References.tsx, RejectBox.tsx, PlayButton.tsx, useAudioShelf.ts and the other app/library/audio/*.ts are unmapped - finding 5 is Lane B only because of that.
